method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, equality-rule reverse paraphrase, exact formula, macro, protected-token and identifier comparison, and reconstruction of every natural-deduction proof tree; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Natural deduction with identity: reflexivity and bidirectional substitution rules, substitutability of identicals, symmetry and transitivity exercises, and a quantified uniqueness derivation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Derivations with identity need extra rules. Identity introduction derives t equals t without premises. Either identity-elimination variant replaces t_1 by t_2 or t_2 by t_1 inside A, given the relevant identity and formula premise.
samples.checks: The heading tokens, all three rule diagrams, argument order, introduction label, both elimination labels and display layout are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The metavariables t, t_1 and t_2 range over closed terms, and identity introduction derives any reflexive identity t equals t outright from no assumptions.
samples.checks: Closedness applies to all three terms, no-premise status is explicit, and the reflexive formula remains unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For closed s and t, A(s) together with s equals t derives A(t) by identity elimination. This is the substitutability of identicals, also called Leibniz's Law.
samples.checks: The premise order, substitution direction, proof-tree formulas, rule label and both names are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercise asks for derivations showing that identity is symmetric and transitive, with both properties universally quantified over their variables.
samples.checks: Every universal quantifier, identity orientation, conjunction, conditional and variable is exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: From the sentence saying that some x is identical to every A-object, derive that any two A-objects are identical. Backward proof search introduces the conditional and two universals, then eliminates the existential major assumption using a temporary witness c. The right subderivation obtains a equals c and b equals c from the universal witness property and the A(a)-and-A(b) assumption, and identity elimination yields a equals b.
samples.checks: Both large proof trees, witness c, discharge labels 1 and 2, universal and existential rule directions, the displayed subderivation for a equals c and the final identity-elimination step are preserved exactly.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The final exercises request a quantified substitutability derivation and a derivation turning existence plus uniqueness into existence of an A-object identical to every A-object.
samples.checks: Both complete quantified formulas, connective scopes and all identity arguments remain source-identical.

source_observations: The frozen source's quantified uniqueness example is internally coherent with the declared bidirectional identity-elimination rules; no upstream defect or correction was identified.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
एकरूपता, बंद पद, सममित, संक्रमक, प्रतिस्थापन and लाइब्निझचा नियम follow the edition's established identity and relation vocabulary; the displayed formulas control the exact formal senses.
The source supplies only the a-equals-c subderivation and leaves the parallel b-equals-c derivation implicit; the Marathi target preserves that scope.
